entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: Africa CDC calls an extraordinary meeting of health ministers
entry.summary: Africa CDC said it will convene an extraordinary meeting of African health ministers on 28 October to strengthen the collective response to the outbreak, AP reported. Its director general said the outbreak demands urgent action and political leadership at the highest level.
entry.content:
Africa CDC said it will convene an extraordinary meeting of African health ministers on 28 October to strengthen the collective response to the outbreak, AP reported. Its director general said the outbreak demands urgent action and political leadership at the highest level.

Sources: AP via U.S. News, AP via Medical Xpress

entry.title: Measles · US: CDC confirms a third measles death
entry.summary: CDC added a third measles death to its national count, up from two. Reuters and Al Jazeera report that CDC confirmed it after the National Center for Health Statistics verified that measles was listed as the underlying cause of death on a death certificate. CDC has not said where the death occurred and says its count could change as reviews continue. Pennsylvania's own count is five.
entry.content:
CDC added a third measles death to its national count, up from two. Reuters and Al Jazeera report that CDC confirmed it after the National Center for Health Statistics verified that measles was listed as the underlying cause of death on a death certificate. CDC has not said where the death occurred and says its count could change as reviews continue. Pennsylvania's own count is five.

Sources: Reuters via Yahoo News, Al Jazeera, The Hill

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: Kenya confirms a ninth Ebola case
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry said one more person tested positive, bringing the total to nine including the first patient, who died. The new case is a contact of the first patient who was already in quarantine. The ministry said all nine cases belong to one cluster, that there is no evidence of transmission outside it, and that 134 of 135 identified contacts were in quarantine. It said the first group of contacts completes 21 days of quarantine on 25 October.

Sources: Al Jazeera, The Washington Post, The Standard (Kenya)

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: Nigeria confirms an imported Ebola case
entry.summary: Nigeria's health ministry confirmed one case of Bundibugyo Ebola in the Federal Capital Territory, in a person with recent travel to Uganda; laboratory confirmation was on 20 October. Officials said 44 contacts had been identified. WHO calls it an imported case and the fifth country to detect the virus since the outbreak was declared, says where and when the person was exposed is not yet known, and advises against restrictions on travel or trade.

entry.title: Mpox · Africa & world: Southern Nevada reports its first clade I mpox case
entry.summary: The Southern Nevada Health District reported the first confirmed clade I mpox case in a Clark County resident. The district said the person has no reported travel exposure, so the source of infection is unclear, and that it has reported 11 clade II cases since August. It said anyone who may have been exposed should contact a health care provider and watch for symptoms for 21 days, and that JYNNEOS vaccine is expected to protect against both clades.

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: DR Congo confirms Ebola in an eighth province, North Ubangi
entry.summary: DR Congo's health ministry said on 18 October that the outbreak has reached North Ubangi province, which borders the Central African Republic, with two cases, one of them fatal, in Wapinda health zone. Reuters and Bloomberg had reported the cases on 15 October before the official statement. AP reports the outbreak has recorded at least 9,400 confirmed cases and more than 4,500 deaths, with Ituri province accounting for almost three quarters of cases.

entry.title: Mpox · Africa & world: South Africa reports 26 mpox cases, four new
entry.summary: South Africa's health department said four new laboratory-confirmed cases brought the total reported since 1 January 2026 to 26, up from 22. Clade information is available for 17 cases: 13 are clade Ib and 4 are clade IIb. Of the 18 cases in the Western Cape, 2 were imported and 16 were linked to local transmission.

Sources: Sowetan, The Citizen, IOL

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: Kenya confirms four more Ebola cases, total seven

entry.title: Cholera · Global: Zambia declares a new cholera outbreak and starts oral vaccination
entry.summary: Zambia's government declared a new cholera outbreak after 304 cases and 11 deaths across seven districts in five provinces, local media reported on 1 October. It is separate from the outbreak the government declared over in July. On 17 October the health ministry's figures, reported by Lusaka Times and Xinhua, were 966 cases and 25 deaths in 12 districts across five provinces, as the country launched an oral cholera vaccination campaign in Lusaka and Chibombo district.
entry.content:
Zambia's government declared a new cholera outbreak after 304 cases and 11 deaths across seven districts in five provinces, local media reported on 1 October. Sources: Diggers, Zambia Monitor, Xinhua, Lusaka Times, Xinhua (July outbreak ended)

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: Africa CDC asks for accountability on over $700 million of response funding
entry.summary: Africa CDC's director general said on 14 October that more than $700 million of Ebola response funding channelled through international partners could not yet be traced to the response, and that the funds were not transferred to the DR Congo government. He asked partners to account for the money, and DR Congo authorities said they would ask the partners concerned for explanations.

Sources: Reuters via AOL, Africanews

entry.title: Cholera · Global: WHO: suspected cholera cases in Yemen roughly triple in three weeks
entry.summary: WHO says Yemen has recorded 8,034 suspected cholera cases and 27 deaths so far this year, and that weekly cases roughly tripled over three weeks. Five governorates hosting large numbers of displaced people (Abyan, Lahij, Al Dhale'e, Taiz and Aden) account for 92% of reported cases. WHO called for funding and access to safe water, vaccination and health services.

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Governor says quarantine lifted and monitoring of all contacts complete
entry.summary: Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev said in a video address on 8 October that the quarantine at Shelekhov District Hospital has been lifted, about a week after the worker's death. Regional media report that Rospotrebnadzor said the full set of preventive measures was completed on 8 October, with medical monitoring finished for all contacts, no health changes linked to infectious disease, and nearly 5,000 laboratory tests that found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms. Officially the cause of death remains "pneumonia of unknown etiology". WHO has not yet said whether it has received the pathogen details it asked for.
entry.content:

Regional media report that Rospotrebnadzor said the full set of preventive measures was completed on 8 October, with medical monitoring finished for all contacts, no health changes linked to infectious disease, and nearly 5,000 laboratory tests that found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms. Officially the cause of death remains "pneumonia of unknown etiology". WHO has not yet said whether it has received the pathogen details it asked for.

Sources: IrCity, EANews, Kyiv Independent, Mediazona, The Moscow Times (Russian service)

entry.title: Plague · Russia: WHO asks Russia for the pathogen, test results and contact details
entry.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros said WHO does not yet have the full picture and cannot conduct a full risk assessment. WHO has asked Russia about the pathogen behind the pneumonia, the lab tests, the contacts and their health, and about media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause. Those reports have not been confirmed by local officials. WHO's initial assessment stands: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. WHO said it has seen no evidence of plague spreading.
entry.content:
WHO Director-General Tedros said WHO does not yet have the full picture and cannot conduct a full risk assessment. WHO has asked Russia about the pathogen behind the pneumonia, the lab tests, the contacts and their health, and about media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause. Those reports have not been confirmed by local officials. WHO's initial assessment stands: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. WHO said it has seen no evidence of plague spreading.

Sources: CNN, The Washington Times

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Rospotrebnadzor: monitoring complete for over 90% of contacts
entry.summary: Russia's consumer safety watchdog said that as of 7 October medical monitoring had been completed for more than 90% of the people who had contact with the worker. It said no health changes linked to infectious disease were detected and that nearly 5,000 laboratory tests found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms. It said there is no risk to residents of Irkutsk and the region. The cause of death remains officially "pneumonia of unknown etiology".
entry.content:
Russia's consumer safety watchdog said that as of 7 October medical monitoring had been completed for more than 90% of the people who had contact with the worker. It said no health changes linked to infectious disease were detected and that nearly 5,000 laboratory tests found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms. It said there is no risk to residents of Irkutsk and the region. The cause of death remains officially "pneumonia of unknown etiology".

Sources: CNN, Fontanka

Media have reported a second institute employee with pneumonia, and some outlets a second death; Russian officials have confirmed neither. WHO has asked Russia to clarify the reports.
